newsitem.title: USA: SBC Communications moves to ease Internet traffic jam.
newsitem.headline: SBC Communications moves to ease Internet traffic jam.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc. said Tuesday it has introduced a technology into its five-state region which will siphon off Internet traffic to head off worries about congestion in the phone network.

The technology, developed with Northern Telecom Ltd. of Canada, recognises and splits off Internet traffic and routes it to a new high-speed network. Currently, voice and data calls share the same network.
The technology is called Internet/Intranet Transport Service (IITS) and will be marketed under the Southwestern Bell brand name to Internet service providers.
"We are enthusiastic about the prospects for this product and the benefits it will bring to our customers," said SBC Chairman Edward Whitacre.
San Antonio-based SBC said the initiative cost less than $100 million.

Some regional Bell executives have complained that upgrading their networks to cope with the 150 percent to 200 percent annual increase in Internet traffic is unfair because they do not get access charges to connect Internet calls.

The average Internet call is 20.8 minutes, compared with 3.8 minutes for an average phone call. Unlike a network designed for data, local phone networks dedicate a whole line for each call, even if little or no data is traversing it.
SBC is in the process of acquiring Pacific Telesis Group, an acquisition that is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter.
PacTel's California territory has had the worst problems with Internet congestion.

Executives at SBC said they could make no plans to extend the technology into California until the acquisition was complete. However, they acknowledged it would be the area where such a technology would be most useful.
SBC's home states are Texas, Kansas, Missouri, Oklahoma and Arkansas.
